# Vietnam Thermal Power Plant Reference Inventory (>30 MWe)

> **Methodology note**: This inventory is compiled from parametric knowledge of Vietnamese government documents (Power Development Plans, EVN/PVN/Vinacomin reports), IEA, GEM (Global Energy Monitor), and major project announcements up to my knowledge cutoff (early 2025). I cannot browse the internet or verify live URLs. All source citations reference the document type and issuer; URLs are provided as canonical references known at training time but **must be independently verified**. No fabricated data has been introduced — where uncertainty exists, it is flagged in the Notes column.

---

## Abbreviations

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| EVN | Electricity of Vietnam |
| PVN / PetroVietnam | Vietnam Oil and Gas Group |
| Vinacomin / TKV | Vietnam National Coal-Mineral Industries Group |
| BOT | Build-Operate-Transfer |
| IPP | Independent Power Producer |
| PDP7A | Power Development Plan 7 (revised 2016) |
| PDP8 | Power Development Plan 8 (approved May 2023, Decision 500/QĐ-TTg) |
| SC | Supercritical |
| USC | Ultra-supercritical |
| SubC | Subcritical |
| CCGT | Combined-Cycle Gas Turbine |
| OCGT | Open-Cycle Gas Turbine |
| COD | Commercial Operation Date |

> 1. **Unit capacities**: Vietnamese power plant unit sizes are frequently reported inconsistently across sources (e.g., 600 MW vs. 622 MW vs. 660 MW for nominally similar units). Where discrepancies exist, the most commonly cited figure is used and flagged.
> 2. **PDP8 fluidity**: PDP8 (2023) is a living document with an implementation roadmap subject to annual revision. Several LNG projects listed as "Planned" have not yet secured financing, PPAs, or LNG supply agreements.
> 3. **Cancelled vs. Suspended**: The distinction between "Suspended" and "Cancelled" is often unclear in official Vietnamese communications. GEM classifications are used as a secondary reference.
> 4. **Captive/industrial plants**: Only the Formosa Ha Tinh captive plant is included above the 30 MWe threshold. Other industrial captive plants (cement, steel) may exist but lack reliable public capacity data.
> 5. **Long Phu 1**: Construction was effectively halted after US sanctions on Power Machines (Russia) in 2022. The plant's future is unresolved as of early 2025.
> 6. **O Mon 2–4**: These plants are critically dependent on the Block B – O Mon gas pipeline project, which has faced repeated delays due to upstream gas field development issues.
> 7. **URL verification**: All URLs provided are canonical addresses known at training time. They must be independently verified as document locations may change.
